query: Resorts World shall deposit cash or bond equal to 5 percent of its proposed total investment by December 31, 2025.

facts.text: The RWNYC license required cash or bond equal to 5% of total investment proposed in its application by December 31, 2025.
The $500 million gaming license fee is a separate obligation from the completion security.
The governing statute permits an approved deposit bond instead of cash.
The official Q&A says a deposit bond must guarantee payment upon default.
In February 2026 the Commission said two unnamed licensees had provided completion bonds and a third bond was being finalized.
The Board reported a recalculated standardized RWNYC capital investment figure of $3.3 billion.
Monetary fields in RWNYC's public capital-investment submission are redacted.
The compiled rules print a 10% deposit figure even though RWNYC's individual license states 5%.
Genting's audited report says GENNY financed the $500 million license fee in January 2026.
The June 2026 company report gives group restricted cash without attributing it to RWNYC's security.

conditions.text: RWNYC supplied cash or an acceptable completion bond to the Commission.
The RWNYC security equaled 5% of its approved total proposed application investment.
The RWNYC security was deposited by December 31, 2025.

reference_verdict.reasoning: Retain partially corroborated, pending human review. Confidence is high for the license obligation: cash or bond equal to 5% of total Application investment by December 31, 2025. RWNYC-specific provision, approved amount and timeliness remain unverified. The unnamed two-licensee bond statement cannot identify RWNYC or exclude cash. Later reviewed records add no receipt; fees, financing and group cash are distinct. Keep the formula uncomputed and avoid double-counting TG-GOLD-A010. Missing public evidence does not establish nonposting or breach.

sources.title: RWNYC Gaming Facility License Award
sources.citation: December 19, 2025 license letter, PDF p.4, Exhibit 1, Conditions 1–2
sources.locator: December 19, 2025 license letter, PDF p.4, Exhibit 1, Conditions 1–2
sources.specific_evidence: Condition 2 requires RWNYC to deposit cash or bond representing 5% of total investment proposed in the Application by December 31, 2025. Condition 1 separately requires the $500 million license fee; the award document does not establish security receipt.
sources.notes: Binding obligation only. Implements TG-GOLD-A010 with a fixed rate and deadline; do not count a second security obligation or equate fee payment with performance.

sources.title: PML 1321-e: Required Capital Investment
sources.specific_evidence: The statute provides for construction security of 5–10% of proposed investment, permits an approved deposit bond instead of cash, and governs escrow, return and forfeiture. It establishes the legal framework without confirming any RWNYC deposit or accepted instrument.
sources.notes: Cash and bond are alternatives. An unidentified unfinished bond cannot establish absence of qualifying cash; the face amount is construction security, not community-benefit spending.

sources.title: Official Round Two Questions and Answers
sources.citation: December 2024 with errata; Q741–744, printed pp.37–39; Q815, printed pp.56–57
sources.publisher: New York State Gaming Facility Location Board
sources.locator: December 2024 with errata; Q741–744, printed pp.37–39; Q815, printed pp.56–57
sources.specific_evidence: The answers explain project-specific rate and timing, identify total Application investment as the calculation base, and require a deposit bond to guarantee payment on default. They do not reconcile RWNYC investment line items or document an accepted RWNYC instrument.
sources.notes: Keep the formula uncomputed. Ordinary letters of credit, borrowing capacity and parent completion guarantees do not independently establish accepted completion security.

sources.title: February 2026 Adopted Commission Minutes
sources.citation: February 3, 2026 meeting, adopted March 16; PDF pp.1 and 4
sources.locator: February 3, 2026 meeting, adopted March 16; PDF pp.1 and 4
sources.specific_evidence: The Commission reported that two of three licensees had provided completion bonds and the third was being finalized. It also discussed the five-percent setting. The minutes identify neither the two providers nor their amounts, posting dates or December deadline compliance.
sources.notes: Do not infer RWNYC's identity from the unnamed pair. Adoption on March 16 is not a posting date; the same-meeting transcript is not independent confirmation.

sources.title: GFLB Report and Findings
sources.citation: March 2026; RWNYC assessment, printed pp.33–34 and applicant capital-investment summary
sources.publisher: New York State Gaming Facility Location Board
sources.locator: March 2026; RWNYC assessment, printed pp.33–34 and applicant capital-investment summary
sources.specific_evidence: The Board reports $3.3 billion of standardized RWNYC capital investment following recalculation and assesses the project. This evaluation figure does not identify the Commission-approved calculation base or principal of the required security, and it is not evidence of receipt.
sources.notes: Do not multiply this evaluation total by 5% as an approved amount. Project financing guarantees and development progress do not establish A061 performance.

sources.title: RWNYC Capital Investment Details
sources.citation: Public application copy, all six pages visually reviewed in completed research
sources.publisher: Genting New York LLC; hosted by New York State Gaming Facility Location Board
sources.locator: Public application copy, all six pages visually reviewed in completed research
sources.specific_evidence: The public capital-investment submission contains redacted monetary fields. Visual review of all six pages did not establish the approved A061 dollar base, a completion-bond principal, a cash receipt or a Commission acceptance date.
sources.notes: The four-page Minimum Capital Investment submission was also visually reviewed and redacted. Advertised $5.5 billion and $7.5 billion totals do not resolve the approved base.

sources.title: NYSGC Compiled Casino Gaming Rules
sources.specific_evidence: The compiled rules continue to print a 10% deposit requirement and address final-construction-stage certification. Official Q&A acknowledged the rate discrepancy. These contextual provisions do not establish RWNYC receipt, override its license's explicit 5% requirement or demonstrate a breach.
sources.notes: Preserve the governing license rate and deadline. The completed review did not resolve the conforming rule history or locate a RWNYC-specific deadline amendment.

sources.title: October 2026 Commission Transcript
sources.citation: October 9, 2026 meeting transcript, 15 pages; latest listed meeting at research cutoff
sources.locator: October 9, 2026 meeting transcript, 15 pages; latest listed meeting at research cutoff
sources.specific_evidence: The reviewed October transcript yielded no bond match or RWNYC-specific security receipt. Selected March, May, July and August Commission records were also screened without identifying RWNYC's deposit. This later coverage did not resolve provision, approved amount or deadline compliance.
sources.notes: Scoped nonfinding only. October minutes were still draft at cutoff; construction and opening updates do not establish security posting or release.

sources.title: Genting Malaysia Berhad FY2025 Audited Financial Report
sources.citation: FY2025; Notes 30 and 40, PDF pp.63 and 72; Note 40 printed p.156
sources.publisher: Genting Malaysia Berhad; company report retrieved through FinancialFilings mirror
sources.locator: FY2025; Notes 30 and 40, PDF pp.63 and 72; Note 40 printed p.156
sources.specific_evidence: The audited report states that GENNY used a credit facility in January 2026 to pay the $500 million commercial casino license fee. Consolidated restricted cash is disclosed without A061 attribution; neither fact establishes RWNYC's completion-security provision or timeliness.
sources.notes: The license fee and completion security are separate obligations. Consolidated cash and financing proceeds cannot identify an accepted cash deposit or bond.

sources.title: Genting Malaysia Berhad Second Quarterly Report 2026
sources.citation: Six months ended June 30, 2026; PDF pp.3 and 11; published August 2026
sources.publisher: Genting Malaysia Berhad; unaudited company report retrieved through FinancialFilings mirror
sources.locator: Six months ended June 30, 2026; PDF pp.3 and 11; published August 2026
sources.specific_evidence: The latest periodic company report identified in the completed review discloses consolidated restricted cash and no material contingent-liability change, without an A061 allocation or receipt. Its period ends June 30, so it cannot establish performance during the remaining months before cutoff.
sources.notes: Group accounting disclosures do not identify the licensee, instrument or acceptance date. No report-specific disclosure is not proof of nonposting; issuer access required mirrors.
